players.product: bring-your-own-power combined-cycle gas generation for hyperscale data centers (1.2 GW Texas project; 5.4 GW of GE Vernova turbine / Kiewit EPC slots)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion, up $308 million or 34% year over year (first full quarter of the LS Power portfolio, higher PJM capacity values, Smart Home growth); free cash flow before growth $1.025 billion, up $111 million; adjusted EPS $1.49 versus $1.73 on acquisition interest and D&A. East adjusted EBITDA +$370 million; Texas -$131 million as ERCOT Houston around-the-clock prices averaged $33/MWh, well below the $52 planning assumption.
quarterly_data.figure: adj EBITDA $1.2 billion (+34%); FCFbG $1.025 billion; adj EPS $1.49

quarterly_data.signal: First bring-your-own-power (BYOP) data-center deal: aligned on principal commercial terms with 'a leading global cloud and AI hyperscaler' including its capital commitment to support 1.2 GW of new combined-cycle gas generation in Texas, with potential to expand to 2.4 GW; NRG will develop, own and operate the plant supporting a 1 GW data center load; initial term at least 15 years; COD targeted late 2029; $3.2 billion of investment ($2,700 a kW, 60% EPC); at full operation $500 million of annual adjusted EBITDA and $375 million of annual free cash flow before growth; pre-tax unlevered IRR within the 12%-15% target, build multiple ~6x. FID still subject to negotiations, land matters and internal approvals.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.2 GW (expandable to 2.4 GW); $3.2 billion capex; $500 million annual EBITDA; COD late 2029

quarterly_data.signal: BYOP commercial structure: an availability-based capacity payment recovers capital and return ('we're paid for the megawatts we build and make available, not for how much the data center runs') and a separate operating payment recovers gas and plant costs; 95% of project free cash flow is supported by capacity payments independent of data-center utilization; customer obligations backed by an investment-grade parent guarantee; the capacity payment 'switches on immediately upon COD'; implied PPA-equivalent 'in the probably $85-$90+ range' per MWh at expected usage.
quarterly_data.figure: 95% of project FCF from capacity payments; ~$85-$90+/MWh equivalent

quarterly_data.signal: Equipment position: the 1.2 GW project is 'the first 1.2 GW of the 5.4 GW of turbine and EPC capacity we've secured through 2032' via GE Vernova and Kiewit; broader development pipeline is more than twice the 5.4 GW secured, 'with every turbine slot tied to an active customer discussion'; under the GE Vernova/Kiewit structure another 1.2 GW block can come online serially each year after the 2029 COD; plus about 2 GW of uprate opportunities across the PJM fleet (less than half economic at the $555/MW-day cap, all 2,000 MW in bilateral talks).
quarterly_data.figure: 5.4 GW turbine + EPC capacity secured through 2032; pipeline >2x that; ~2 GW PJM uprates

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 capital plan adds a $721 million data center new build investment category (of which $681 million is incremental, funded by lower liability management); the vast majority of 2026 spend is turbine equipment procurement that could be redeployed to other projects ('not sunk cost'); cumulative investment $0.8 billion through 2026 including reservation payments, then $1 billion in 2027, $1.1 billion in 2028 and $0.3 billion in 2029; $1 billion annual share repurchase commitment unchanged; 3x leverage target pushed from 2028 to 2029 if funded on balance sheet, with capital-partner structures under evaluation.

Reaffirmed 2026 guidance but tracking below the midpoint on soft Texas load/prices and Winter Storm Fern supply costs; Virginia rejoining RGGI adds an estimated $70 million of 2026 cost on the 1.2 GW of acquired Virginia assets; core business still expected to deliver 14%+ adjusted EPS CAGR through 2030 before any data-center projects; illustrative 2030 contracted free cash flow of $1.2 billion including the BYOP project.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 guidance reaffirmed (below midpoint); 14%+ adj EPS CAGR through 2030; 2030 contracted FCF ~$1.2 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Delivery track record and next steps: 1.5 GW Texas Energy Fund portfolio on track with T.H. Wharton delivered on time and on budget; NRG targeted at least 1 GW of large load agreements in 2026 and the BYOP deal would meet that; Texas policy is moving toward customer-backed new supply ('new demand should be matched with new generation'), and ERCOT forwards are not yet pricing data-center load — 'until it's real, it's not'.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.5 GW Texas Energy Fund portfolio; >=1 GW large-load target for 2026
